claims.text: The feedstock is a FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy powder.
The feedstock has a 15–45 μm particle-size distribution.
The 15–45 μm feedstock previously produced high-quality but insufficiently thick coatings with the HVAF-i7 system.
Increasing the HVAF-i7 stand-off distance to approximately 300–350 mm will increase particle impact velocity.
Optimizing the stand-off distance to 300–350 mm will overcome the coating-thickness limitation.
The proposed distance adjustment will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation and coating integrity.
Greater particle kinetic energy improves splat formation and deposition efficiency.
A longer spray distance gives particles more time to accelerate before impact.
Higher particle momentum improves adhesion and coating packing density.
Improved adhesion and packing density lead to a thicker and more robust coating.
Higher particle speed reduces in-flight particle oxidation.
Reducing residence time over the substrate preserves the desired coating microstructure.
The intervention will produce a significantly thicker, adherent bond coat with oxidation and microstructural integrity comparable to the HVAF-M3 baseline.
The intervention should remain effective for deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
The intervention should remain effective during high-temperature thermal-barrier service provided that the environment does not alter the improved particle kinetic profile.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome invokes the HVAF-M3 process as the comparison baseline, whereas the baseline field defines the control as HVAF-i7 at the original spray distance.

A required stand-off distance of 300–350 mm is not reconciled with deposition inside a 120 mm internal diameter; no torch orientation or access geometry is specified that would make both constraints simultaneously achievable.
